This subsection is an engineering conformance example, not a benchmark result. The installed public demo (\path{examples/public-regression}) fits the UCI Airfoil Self-Noise table (Brooks, Pope, and Marcolini; CC~BY~4.0; DOI 10.24432/C5VW2C) on a grouped development split ($1{,}190$ fit rows and $313$ query rows, seed $1729$) and writes one native raw-unit artifact, a \texttt{DOPERAW1} file (SHA-256 \texttt{0950cbe79817\ldots}) with profile \texttt{raw-numeric-symbolic-v1} under the byte profile \texttt{native-raw-complete-v1}. Compile, \texttt{inspect}, the research receipt, and the file size all report 1{,}558 bytes: 56 bytes of native framing, 1{,}080 bytes of fitted schema and transforms, and 422 bytes of sampling payload. The file is its own transport archive, so every dataset-specific dependency of sampling is charged once inside it. The generic runtime is measured separately: the debug binary and its mapped libraries came to 72{,}049{,}152 bytes, so the cold sampling closure was 72{,}050{,}710 bytes. No portable bundle or release-build runtime was measured. The run used commit \texttt{59437b1}, and privacy, driver, and geometry checks are unmeasured for this artifact. It is a different object from the benchmark charge (the encoded \texttt{.dpk} file plus \texttt{projection.json}) and from the README toy, and no number in the panel comes from it. \path{docs/whitepaper/receipts/native-byte-conformance-v1.json} pins these values.
